scope: read-only source review of the integrated real device onboarding feature against docs/architecture/real-device-onboarding.md
method: delegated automated source review by a read-only review agent, executed against the canonical working tree
note: this is an additional automated review pass; it is not an independent human reviewer and it does not replace one
execution_evidence: none: the review was source reading only, no build, test, database or network access
areas_with_no_defect_found: no cookie-only mutation path: every cookie authorized mutating route requires exact Origin and x-oip-csrf
GET /api/v2/browser/session does not leak the CSRF value to an unauthenticated caller and the server has no CORS layer
session tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests, cookies are host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ with the session TTL
SSE revalidates the browser session for every projection
no shell is used for SSH; every argument is a separate argv entry, hosts and users are validated
subprocess deadlines, output bounds, kill/wait on cancellation and pinned known_hosts handling are in place
UID 0 and unverifiable UIDs are rejected before authentication verification and before every fact query
plan ownership, plan expiry and the 64/4 plan limits are enforced
the source limit of 32 is validated against the complete prospective hierarchy before any SQL
only the daemon opens the SqliteStore; foreign keys are enforced and deferred to commit
device_connection_audit has no update or delete path in application code
no handler, adapter or MCP tool can supply a Principal, a grant, a private key path or a fabricated verification fact

findings.defect: The server never enforces the contract rule that RSA keys require at least 2048 bits. ssh-keygen -lf already prints the key size but only the fingerprint is kept; enforcement is delegated to the RequiredRSASize=2048 ssh client option of the user connection. A weak ssh-rsa host key can be scanned, displayed, explicitly trusted and pinned.
findings.suggested_fix: parse the key size from the ssh-keygen -lf output in ssh::scan/pin_file and reject ssh-rsa keys below 2048 bits with a typed fault before the key is offered or pinned; keep RequiredRSASize as defence in depth
findings.fix: The server parses the size of every offered host key itself and rejects a key below the accepted minimum before it is offered for acceptance or pinned. The attempt fails with SSH_HOST_KEY_TOO_WEAK and no binding is created.

findings.defect: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED and Host key verification failed are both mapped to SSH_HOST_KEY_CHANGED, so an unknown host key is reported as a host key rotation alarm.
findings.suggested_fix: map only REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED to SSH_HOST_KEY_CHANGED and give the unknown key case its own code and status
findings.fix: Only REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED maps to SSH_HOST_KEY_CHANGED. An unpinned host reports SSH_HOST_KEY_UNKNOWN and the operator status host_key_unknown. The split was verified against the installed OpenSSH 10.2 with an owned loopback fixture.

findings.defect: The invalid code limiter is evaluated before the grant lookup, so sixteen malformed codes block the operator's valid single use code for sixty seconds. The exposure is limited to local processes because require_origin keeps cross site browsers out.
findings.suggested_fix: evaluate the failure gate after the grant lookup and use a decaying per source limiter so a legitimate code can never be blocked
findings.fix: The rejection accounting is bounded at 16 entries and is evaluated after the grant lookup, so earlier invalid attempts never block a valid single-use grant.

findings.defect: The maximal host report the parser can build exceeds the 128 KiB payload_json CHECK of device_connections, so a legal but extreme remote report fails the commit with an opaque storage error instead of a typed fault.
findings.suggested_fix: reconcile the parser bound with the schema bound and length check the serialised record before the transaction so the failure is typed
findings.fix: The parser charges every collected disk name, mount, interface name and address against a report budget and refuses an oversized report with SSH_OUTPUT_LIMIT. Before the write the server compares the serialised record with the shared domain bound and refuses a record that cannot be stored with SSH_REPORT_TOO_LARGE, so no partial binding is created. The storage schema keeps its bound and a test proves that both use the same value.

findings.defect: The read path of GET /api/v2/device-connections?plan_id=... requires DeviceConnectionConfigure, while the contract places that read under DeviceConnectionRead. Conservative over restriction, not a privilege escalation.
findings.suggested_fix: parameterise the plan check with the capability id, Read for the query path and Configure for the action paths
findings.next_step: Deliberately paused: the change loosens a permission and is a security decision, not a conformance fix. It needs an explicit release, a negative test for a foreign principal and a principal without InventoryManage, and a parity update.

findings.defect: The session capacity check runs after the single use grant was already removed, so a valid code is destroyed when 64 sessions exist.
findings.suggested_fix: check the session capacity before removing the grant and evict expired sessions first
findings.fix: The session capacity is checked before the grant is removed, so a full session table no longer consumes an issued grant.

findings.defect: The SSH work directory is created with the process umask and only afterwards chmod'ed to 0700, which leaves a brief world readable window. The content is public host keys only.
findings.suggested_fix: create the directory with DirBuilder::mode(0o700) so the mode is set atomically with creation
findings.fix: The private work directory is created with the owner-only mode and the exact mode is re-asserted afterwards, so it is never briefly world readable.

test_gaps.gap: No Rust level test covers the browser session, CSRF and Origin flow; those assertions exist only in the external harness tests/real_device/acceptance.py.
suggested_tests: cookie only POST without x-oip-csrf on /api/v2/device-connections is rejected
cookie only POST without x-oip-csrf on /api/v2/inventory/apply is rejected
a wrong x-oip-csrf value is rejected
a session revoked during an SSE stream stops the delivery of projections
GET /api/v2/browser/session without a cookie returns csrf_token null
test_gaps.fix: crates/oip-server/tests/browser_session.rs adds five Rust integration tests: exact Origin, single-use pairing code, CSRF on every cookie authorized write, revoked session and revoked projection stream.

planned_next_step: N3 in docs/OIP_RELEASE_PROGRESS.md: the OIP-009 browser session, SSE and global context contract, which may only describe what is implemented. N1b/F5 stays paused until an explicit release of the permission change.
review_note: The findings below were produced by an automated read-only review pass. The fixes in fc828ac were implemented and verified by the implementing session, not by an independent reviewer.
